title: The New Covenant of the Spirit
english: …completely, easily, and very readily rejected. And indeed, God said, 'This people approaches me with their mouth and honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me; they worship me in vain, teaching the commandments of men' (Matthew 15:8-9). But our Lord Jesus Christ writes holy and divine laws for us on fleshy, that is, sensible, tablets of the heart. For He also spoke through the prophet Ezekiel, saying, 'I will remove their stony heart from their flesh and give them a fleshy heart, so that they may walk in my commandments' (Ezekiel 36:26). If someone, therefore, does not cling to the shadows through Moses, nor even have the law written in black on stone tablets, but rather has it in the mind through the Spirit, this is the letter of Christ known to all people.

What is the confidence we have through Christ towards God? Listen, then, to one approaching and saying: 'Not that we are sufficient from ourselves to think anything as from ourselves; for all wisdom is from the Lord' (1 Corinthians 4:2; James 1:17), as it is written: 'Every perfect gift is from above and from the Father of lights' (James 1:17). But the one through whom all things are, and in whom all things are, Christ, who mediates for us and for God through the economy, while working all things from God the Father, being both wisdom and power of His own being; what, then, is the confidence through Christ towards God? Listen, then, to one approaching and saying: 'Not that we are sufficient from ourselves to think anything as from ourselves; for all wisdom is from the Lord' (1 Corinthians 4:2), as it is written: 'For all wisdom is from the Lord' (James 1:17). But our sufficiency is from God, who has made us ministers of the new covenant, not of the letter but of the spirit; for the letter kills, but the spirit gives life. And what is the letter? In the law, it is a type, the things still being fulfilled in shadows; but the spirit is the power of the worship in Christ, declaring those approaching it through faith to be spiritual. As much as the type is inferior to the truth, so much, I think, are those serving it inferior to those performing the truth. For Christ sprinkles us with his own blood, and not only for the purity of the flesh, as also the things in the law, but rather he also cleanses our conscience from dead works and removes transgression; and he grants, in addition to this, the hope of life. For it is true that 'the one believing in the Son has eternal life' (John 3:36); for he has promised also the resurrection of their bodies and the restoration to incorruption and to a long life. For the glorified thing will not have been glorified in this part, because of the surpassing glory.

He refers again to the comparison of the axiom of the divine apostleship against the ministries, having made the comparison of the two and having brought forth their own, making more manifest the one in Christ through the spirit. And the scope of his thought comes through these things, but the statement is full yet not very clearly expressed; for it seems to be somehow not very easy to see, nor even ready for those who wish to see. What is the meaning of 'the glorified has not been glorified' and the following? There is something of this kind that he intends to make manifest. For Moses has been glorified, he says, as a minister of the law that is being abolished, but the glory of the new proclamation in Christ, overcoming the first, made it seem as if it had not been glorified at all. Just as when night is still present and the whole universe is grieving under its darkness, the circle of the moon flashes, but the chorus of the stars has its own glory …
translator_notes: The text ends mid-sentence with '...ἡλίου γεμὴν'
The phrase 'the glorified has not been glorified' is a translation of 'οὐδε δεδόξασται τὸ δεδοξασμένον'.
baehrens: PG 74; Fragmenta in 2 Cor u02 rem early

title: Glory of Ministry
english: The glory of the ministry of the law, although it has been overshadowed by the surpassing glory of the gospel, still has a certain glory. However, this glory is not as great as the glory of the gospel, for the lesser always gives way to the greater. If what is being abolished, such as the shadow and the law, has glory, how much more will what remains, the ordinances of God, have glory?

The disciples of Christ have a greater glory, because the word of the gospel has been made clear and simple to them, without anything difficult, unlike the ministry of Moses. Having such hope, we use great boldness, for we are sufficient ministers of the new covenant, not of the letter, but of the Spirit. It is fitting for such ministers to speak with boldness, not being ashamed of the types, nor of the foolishness of the hearers.

The sons of Israel, despite witnessing numerous wonders, proved to be unapproved, and Moses was forced to put a veil on himself when speaking to them about the divine law. This veil was a symbol of the riddles and mysteries that shrouded the true face of the law, which is none other than Christ. The Israelites were unable to gaze upon this glory, and instead, they saw only a faint reflection, a shadow without substance. This shadow, along with the type and figure it represented, has been abolished, for the new covenant has been fulfilled, and Christ is the culmination of the law.

The hidden glory of Moses, which is Christ, was the ultimate goal of the law, and those who remove the veil of the shadow and the second face, as if written in scripture, will behold Emmanuel, who is formed in many ways in each individual, and who suffered and saved the world, enduring the slaughter for the world and rescuing the heavenly. As a result, he will be glorified by us and worshiped by the holy angels. However, the light of the Savior's glory remains inaccessible to the Jewish mind, which is unable to approach the faith in Christ.

The law serves as a guide, leading us to Christ, whereas something else guides us towards what is better and greater than ourselves. This is why the apostle Paul views the things in the law as worthless, considering them rubbish in comparison to the surpassing knowledge of Christ. The Lord is the Spirit, and it is in the Spirit that we find freedom.

To truly see Christ, who is the culmination of what is being abolished - namely, the law - we must become spiritual. Only then can the veil be completely removed, allowing us to see the holy Moses with an unveiled face, the face or shadow that comes from the letter.
